pages.title: Casimir Plate
pages.text: Two conducting plates held nanometres apart. Between them only short vacuum modes fit, so the empty space outside pushes harder than the empty space inside, and the plates are drawn together by nothing at all. Holding the pair, I can feel them straining toward each other.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)To test the Casimir effect properly I needed plates flatter than atoms. Neutronium plate, spaced with slivers of Cherenkov Quartz, made it in the press, and the attraction matched the prediction to the last digit.
